NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The maintainer's ruling, recorded 2026-09-12: "C1, narrow." Three live findings are this bundle's Problem, and two of the three moved since they were written.
F197 (measured 2026-09-08 at 54e26d9) named two prose payment paths in scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts. One of them — a pass over every archived spec.xml matching PAID_FINDING_RE — is gone from the shipped code (PAID_FINDING_RE is defined and used nowhere in src/ or scripts/ code; the name's only two occurrences are fixture data reproducing a finding body, at scripts/fixtures/record-parse/input/findings.xml:7605 and scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/findings.xml:7523). The remaining path is closedWithTokens, which reads an archived row's StatusText and mints every F-token in a sentence beginning "Closed with". The narrow ruling: delete that path, and declare in the same three rows' Pays every payment it currently mints, so the derivation is byte-identical before and after. Measured with the shipped derivePayerMap over the real archive (93 directories) and both registry layers (12 live + 50 retired rows): the full map mints 93 tokens, the Pays-only map 84, and the nine prose-only tokens are F100 F101 F102 F103 F104 F105 (C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE), F112 F113 (C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT) and F125 (C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND). Re-running the comparison with the prose loop deleted and the nine declared in those rows' Pays reproduces the production map exactly (93 of 93 tokens, every payer equal), which is the byte-identity the ruling requires.
F198 (measured 2026-09-08 at 54e26d9) said the bundle that settled F172 had no row. Its headline is history: registry-retired.xml carries a kind="historical" row named C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 whose Pays is F172, and F172 is retired with PaidBy C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2. What is still owed is F198's own payment. The bundle that did that work is C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 (PR #81), whose own Problem measured the rowless population F198 demanded (55 archived bundles with no row in either layer) and whose Summary names the C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 row it wrote. C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 has zero rows in either layer; the house form for exactly that case is a historical row in registry-retired.xml ("This row exists so the derivation can see the payment"). The derivation keys on a row whose name equals an archive directory, so this row mints the moment it exists and F198 becomes eligible mid-bundle.
F185 (measured 2026-09-06, post-archive of C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY) recorded a real-repository measurement test with no explicit timeout. The fix landed in commit 1896592 (PR #75, the C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY merge) as a one-line change to src/grace-context.test.ts: `});` became `}, 30_000);` at line 559. That bundle's row already exists, retired, kind="chartered"; appending F185 to its Pays is the route, with C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2's correction of the retired C-CODIFY-DECISIONS row as precedent. F185 becomes eligible mid-bundle for the same reason.
The trap the brief names is real and was driven: a finding paid through an already-archived bundle's name is eligible the moment the row exists, and the shipped validator exits 1 until --retire moves it. Driven on a whole-repository copy with the proposed edits: validator exit 1 naming exactly F185 (archive event C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY) and F198 (archive event C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2); one --retire reports moved 2; validator exit 0. The bundle's own row pays only at the close, when its name becomes an archive directory: driven, the close's --retire reports moved 2 (F197 and the row) and the validator exits 0.
Two suite failures were discovered by driving the proposed record state, and neither is named in the brief: the payer-derivation baseline (F185, F198, F197 are not in baseline ∪ bundleMinted) and the shipped C-FLUSH-AND-PAY production clamp test, whose third clause asserts headroom is below 7x the median live element line count. That clause is a state claim the ratified arithmetic (C-ROOT-WINDOW-2/-3: the moved ceiling is min(previous ceiling, pre-move base + floored headroom), ceilingBase = findingsBaseRead) falsifies by construction — the formula ceiling is computed from the pre-move base so a retire frees the moved lines, making headroom = 7x median + lines moved whenever the clamp binds. Measured on the driven copy: mid-bundle headroom 249 against product 238, post-close headroom 266 against 238. The other two clauses are exactly what the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 roots-invariant tripwire already asserts for all four roots, so the test is a duplicate (F116's class) under a title that claims a clamp it does not assert; this bundle deletes it and names the tripwire as the carrier. The defect is staged as F244, and F244's payment is recorded at its flush by appending F244 to this bundle's retired row — the same retired-row append this bundle establishes for F185. Both suite changes are forced by this bundle's own state.

Alternatives.Alternative: F198's payer — variant A (chosen): a kind="historical" row named C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 in registry-retired.xml, Pays F198, in the house form, because that bundle did the work and has no row. Pros: matches the established historical-row form used for eight rowless payers by C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 and for C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 by C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2; the derivation keys on the archived name; the witness (the C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 row, F172's retirement, and C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2's own population measurement) is checkable without judgement. Cons: forces a mid-bundle --retire, because C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 is already archived.

F198's payer — variant B (rejected): this bundle's own row pays F198, so it moves at the close. Pros: no mid-bundle move for F198; one fewer record write. Cons: it attributes to C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY work C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 performed, which is the false-payment shape C-PAYMENT-RECORD was chartered to end; and it leaves C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 with a second unrecorded payment while the record is being repaired for exactly that defect. The brief's own reading — "the bundle that paid it has no row" — points at the historical row.

F185's payer — variant A (chosen): append F185 to the retired C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY row's Pays. Pros: the row already exists and names the bundle whose PR carried the fix; the append is one cell edit; C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2 already corrected a retired row's Pays, so the move is lawful in precedent. Cons: a retired row is edited, which is normally immutable; the precedent makes it lawful, and the edit changes only the derived payment set.

F185's payer — variant B (rejected): a historical row named C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY, Pays F185. Cons: it duplicates an identity that already has a row, so the "exactly once across the layers" walks would see two rows for one name — a collision the record's own shape rules exist to prevent. The historical form is for a bundle with no row, not for one that has a retired row.

The StatusText F-token rule — variant A (chosen): no validator rule is owed. Once closedWithTokens is deleted, a token mentioned in StatusText mints nothing, so a rule forbidding F-tokens in StatusText would protect nothing. Per-bundle row-invariant tests that assert the row's StatusText is house-form prose may stay and may still be asserted for a new row; they are style checks, not payment law. Measured population: 14 rows across both layers carry an F-token in StatusText; three of them carried a "Closed with" sentence and minted (the nine tokens above), eleven merely mention.

The StatusText F-token rule — variant B (rejected): add a general validator rule reddening any StatusText that names an F-token. Rejected because it would red 14 rows immediately, eleven for a mere mention, and would convert a harmless prose citation into a hard error; the record's own historical form puts F-tokens in StatusText (four historical rows do).

The C-FLUSH-AND-PAY production clamp test — variant A (chosen): delete the test. Its two durable relations (base + headroom = ceiling, base = newlineCount) are already asserted for all four roots by the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 roots-invariant tripwire, so keeping it reduced is a duplicated assertion (F116's class), and the title "clamp invariant" would claim a clamp it does not assert. Pros: no false title, no duplicate; the clamp behaviour stays driven by the synthetic-fixture clamp tests (T-002 removal, probe 3, the window and anti-ratchet tests); the tripwire is the one carrier of the two relations. Cons: the production record loses a test that was green in its shape, which is the point — its third clause was never an invariant.

The C-FLUSH-AND-PAY production clamp test — variant B (rejected): keep it, renamed to "findings root relations", with a stated reason the tripwire does not cover. There is no such reason: the tripwire asserts base + headroom = ceiling and base = newlineCount for all four live roots, which is the whole of the reduced test, so the rename would leave a duplicate under an accurate title. Rejected as F116's class.

F240 (review.confidently-wrong on an active file-creating plan's Target MustExist), F242 (tsconfig.json includes only src/**) and F243 (a per-task Verification git diff written cumulatively) are staged in .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md and are not this bundle's; the buffer is read-only here. Scenarios.Scenario: Mid-bundle (driven on a whole-repository copy): the three retired rows' Pays carry the nine tokens; C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's Pays carries F185; a kind="historical" row named C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 with Pays F198 sits retired; registry.xml carries the live C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY row with Pays F197. After --rewrite-roots the registry root reads base="13" headroom="13" ceiling="26". The validator exits 1 naming exactly F185 and F198; F197 is not eligible (the bundle's row name is not yet an archive directory). One --retire reports moved 2; findings root 7597/249/7846; index 271/25/296; validator exit 0.

Close (record mechanics driven on the same copy with the bundle's directory present under the archive — the state the shipped apply reaches; the apply drive belongs to the plan's post-close task): the C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY row's name is now an archive directory, so F197 mints. One --retire reports moved 2 (F197 and the row); findings root 7569/266/7835; registry back to 12/14/26; F197 retired with PaidBy C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY; validator exit 0.

Prose-dead probe, both directions (driven on the copy): current code, a live F999 finding plus a "Closed with F999" sentence in an archived row's StatusText reddens the validator at finding-eligible-still-live (archive event C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2, exit 1); with the closedWithTokens loop removed from derivePayerMap the same tree validates exit 0. A planted Pays F999 row still mints F999, so the instrument is not vacuous.

Byte-identity (driven by function): derivePayerMap over the production record mints 93 tokens; over the copy with the prose loop removed and the nine declared in Pays it mints 95 (the same 93 with every payer equal, plus F185 and F198); no production token is missing and no payer differs.
